name: Joe Leaves the Hotel with His Suitcase
description: Joe walks out of the hotel, carrying his suitcase with him.
related_events: Joe departs from the hotel with his suitcase

name: Joe Laughs, Blushes, and Checks His Hair
description: Joe laughs, his face flushing as he turns to the mirror and runs a hand through his hair, adjusting it carefully.
related_events: Joe laughs and checks his hair in the mirror

name: The Manager Demands Joe Buck's Whereabouts
description: The pink manager scowls as he flips open his pocket watch. He looks around, then mutters sharply, 'Where's that Joe Buck?'
related_events: Manager checks pocket watch and expresses frustration about Joe Buck's absence

name: Prostitute Confronts Soldier Over Lost Income
description: A plump, aging prostitute laughs up into the camera, turning her attention to the soldier. She shakes her head, waving a finger at him. 'Hey, hey, what you try to do to me? You gonna cost me money, soldier!'
related_events: Prostitute confronts soldier about potential loss of income

name: Anastasia Clutches Joe and Declares Her Love
description: Anastasia grabs a younger Joe tightly, her eyes wide and breath ragged. She gasps out that he is the only one, the only person she has ever loved.
related_events: Anastasia expresses desperate affection to Joe

name: Bus Stops at Station
description: From a high angle, the bus slows down and comes to a complete stop.
related_events: Bus slows to a stop

name: Packing the Cowboy Outfit
description: Joe hums to himself as he places a full set of cowboy clothes, still wrapped and unworn, into a shiny new suitcase made of black and white horsehide. He calls out, 'Yeah, where's that Joe Buck?'
related_events: Joe packs cowboy clothes into a new suitcase

name: Joe's Reflection in the Bus Window
description: Joe's reflection appears in the bus window as he looks out. He raises his arms as if holding a lasso, swings it in a wide arc, and says he's going to rope the whole island.
related_events: Joe speaks through bus window reflection

name: Moderator Asks if Science Can Replace Stressed Men
description: The Moderator looks into the camera and asks whether American innovation can create a marketable male to replace the men who are stressing themselves into an early grave over women's growing sexual demands.
related_events: Moderator poses question about American know-how and male replacement

name: Waitress Looks for Joe Buck
description: The waitress, sweating, glances up and asks where Joe Buck is.
related_events: Waitress glances up while sweating
Waitress asks about Joe Buck's location

name: Moderator Introduces the Masculinity Crisis
description: The moderator stands before the camera, addressing the audience directly. He states that masculinity is a topic many people regard as inappropriate, unimportant, or a subject of ridicule. Despite this, he suggests that the issue may point to a deeper societal problem. He describes a growing sense of tension among American men, noting that one in four feels anxious or challenged by the changing dynamics in relationships, particularly in response to increased sexual expectations from women. With this, he introduces the subject of the evening's discussion.
related_events: moderator introduces topic of masculinity crisis

name: Sally Buck Wipes Lipstick and Warns Joe
description: Sally Buck gently wipes lipstick from Joe's lips, then looks at him and tells him to keep his hands off her operators.
related_events: Sally Buck wipes lipstick from Joe's lips
Sally Buck warns Joe to keep hands off her operators

name: Manager Reprimands Employee for Late Arrival and Dirty Dishes
description: The Manager stands holding his watch, his finger wagging toward the camera. He glances at the time, then gestures sharply toward a pile of dirty dishes. 'You're due here at four o'clock. Look at those dishes, look!' he says, his voice firm and pointed.
related_events: Manager points to watch and scolds while gesturing at dishes

name: Woodsy Sings Drunkenly on the Bed
description: Woodsy sits cross-legged on the bed, naked except for his Stetson and a guitar. He sings in a drunken voice while Little Joe lies under the covers, held in Sally Buck's arms. The room is quiet except for his off-key serenade.
related_events: Woodsy sings drunkenly while sitting naked on the bed

name: Joe Starts Singing with Veterans
description: Joe slapped one of the Veterans on the back and began singing, 'Off we go, into the wild blue yonder,' and the group joined in, trying to follow the song.
related_events: Joe slaps a Veteran on the back
Group attempts to sing 'Off we go, into the wild blue yonder'

name: Veterans Exit Bus and Take Down Banners
description: The veterans began to leave the bus, stepping down one by one. As they disembarked, they carefully took down the banners and flags mounted on the bus, carrying them with them as they moved away.
related_events: Veterans prepare to disembark from the bus
Veterans remove banners and flags from the bus

name: Joe Leans Across the Marines to Watch as Veterans Sing 'Anchors Aweigh'
description: Joe shifted forward, leaning across the two Marines seated beside him to look out the window. At the same time, the Veterans in the vehicle began singing 'Anchors Aweigh, my boys, anchors aweigh.' The sound filled the space as Joe remained focused on the view outside.
related_events: Joe leans across two Marines to look out the window
Veterans begin singing 'Anchors Aweigh'

name: Joe Offers a Cigarette, Cowhand Declines
description: Joe shakes his head, grinning, and offers the old Cowhand a cigarette. The old Cowhand shakes his head in refusal, holding up the cigarette Joe had already lit for him to show it is still burning.
related_events: Joe offers a cigarette to the old Cowhand
Old Cowhand declines the cigarette offer

name: Joe Puts On His Cowboy Boots and Adjusts His Cuffs
description: Joe sings as he pulls on his new cowboy boots. He tugs at the cuffs of his pants to reveal the yellow sunburst pattern at the ankle. The scene holds in a still image as the credits begin.
related_events: Joe sings while putting on his cowboy boots
Joe adjusts his cuffs to reveal the sunburst design

name: Ralph Confronts Dirty Dishes and Calls for Joe Buck
description: Ralph stands in the kitchen, staring at a large pile of dirty dishes stacked in the sink and on the counter. He shakes his head slightly, then turns away, calling out, "Where's that Joe Buck?" His voice carries through the room, firm and edged with impatience.
related_events: Ralph confronts pile of dirty dishes
Ralph calls out for Joe Buck

name: Joe Passes the Bottle as Veterans Sing
description: Joe laughed as he passed the bottle, his hands moving easily, the laughter blending with the first notes of the veterans' song. They began singing 'The Caissons Go Rolling Along,' their voices rising together, filling the air with rhythm and memory. The group's attention turned toward the music, bodies swaying slightly, as the sound carried over the gathering.
related_events: Joe passes the bottle while laughing
Veterans begin singing 'Caissons Go Rolling Along'

name: Sally Buck Teases Joe in the Salon
description: Joe sits on the couch, flipping through a magazine. Sally Buck leans over a young woman, bleaching her hair roots. She glances at Joe and says the groom won’t find out the bride isn’t a real blonde until after the wedding, then it’ll be too late. Joe laughs. Sally turns to him, feigning sternness, and tells him he’s getting too big for his britches.
related_events: Joe sits on couch reading magazine
Sally Buck bleaches young woman's hair
Sally Buck warns Joe about growing too confident

name: Joe Dresses and Sings Before Answering Ralph
description: Joe buttons his new cowboy shirt, singing as he moves about. He pauses the song to answer a call from Ralph. After the interruption, he resumes singing while pulling up and zipping his tight black slacks. The moment he finishes, the singing and image freeze as the CREDITS begin.
related_events: Joe buttons his new cowboy shirt while singing
Joe interrupts his song to answer Ralph
Joe resumes singing while pulling up and zipping his black slacks
Singing and image freeze for CREDITS

name: Joe Wakes and Says Goodbye to the Old Cowhand
description: Joe wakes up stiff and disoriented, rubbing his neck as he straightens in his seat. He sees the Old Cowhand lifting a sweat-stained saddle from the overhead rack and walking toward the front of the bus. Joe calls out, 'Nice talking to you, old timer.' The Old Cowhand steps off the bus. Joe pulls a stick of gum from his pocket, pops it into his mouth, and turns to wave through the window as the bus pulls away.
related_events: Joe awakens with a stiff neck and becomes alert
Old Cowhand removes saddle from overhead rack
Joe calls farewell to the Old Cowhand
Joe chews gum and waves out the window

name: Joe Locks His Suitcase and Leaves with a Defiant Smile
description: Joe locks his suitcase and laughs, saying he knows what can be done with the dishes, adding that if the other person isn't willing to do it, he’ll take care of it himself. He picks up the suitcase and a portable transistor radio, walks away from the mirror, then stops to comb his hair, tuck a cigarette into the corner of his mouth, and light it with a match struck against his thumbnail. He turns back for one last look at himself in the mirror, standing proud and still, then leaves.
related_events: Joe locks his suitcase before departure
Joe speaks defiantly about doing the dishes
Joe adjusts his appearance before leaving

name: Woodsy Laughs at Little Joe's Balancing Act and Quotes Cowboy Ideals
description: Little Joe stands in front of the trough, lifting one foot off the ground as he tries to balance on the other. Woodsy watches, wearing his new Stetson, and bursts into loud laughter. Still chuckling, he tips his hat slightly and says that he-men stand and shoot from the hip.
related_events: Little Joe attempts to balance on one foot in front of the trough
Woodsy laughs loudly at Little Joe's balancing attempt
Woodsy declares that real men stand and shoot from the hip

name: Joe Walks Out Amid Whistles and a Farewell Song
description: The door marked EMPLOYEES ONLY swings open and Joe steps out, crossing the sterile white dining room. He moves past greasy dishes piled with garbage, steam trays holding limp food, coffee-soaked cigarette butts, and formica tables smeared with dried ketchup and mustard. Two pimply high school girls watch him, slurping noisily through the straws of their empty coke glasses. From off-screen, a chorus begins to sing: "From this valley they say you are going -- we will miss your bright eyes and sweet smile for they say you are taking the sunshine..."
related_events: Joe emerges from employees-only area and walks through dining room
Two high school girls react to Joe with suggestive straw noises
Off-screen chorus begins singing farewell ballad

name: Joe Sings and Dresses with Playful Energy
description: Wrapped in a towel, Joe stands in front of his dresser mirror singing as he sprays deodorant on himself, then playfully aims a puff toward his crotch. He freezes in place, the song cutting off abruptly as the image pauses. The scene shifts to him tearing the wrapping from a new Stetson hat and setting it on his head, the moment again freezing as the credits continue to roll.
related_events: Joe sings while preparing in front of mirror
Joe applies deodorant playfully
Joe unveils and wears new Stetson hat

name: Joe Leaves the Cafeteria and Walks to the Bus Depot
description: Joe finishes his meal and steps out of the cafeteria. He begins walking along the street of a small Western town, heading toward the bus depot. The sound of his boots clicks and clacks against the pavement, echoing loudly in the quiet air. A radio at his ear broadcasts grain prices from the Commodity Exchange. As he walks, the town stretches ahead—weathered buildings, scattered vehicles, and signs of slow growth. His pace slows as he passes through the stillness of the afternoon.
related_events: Joe finishes eating and leaves the cafeteria
Joe begins walking toward the bus depot

name: Joe Walks Through Town with Grain Prices on the Radio
description: Joe walks down the street of a small Western town, the click-clack of his boots echoing as he makes his way toward the bus depot. The radio at his ear crackles with a steady drone of grain prices from the Commodity exchange. He passes storefronts and empty lots, the town quiet, caught between its past and the slow push of urbanization. The broadcast continues, a steady stream of numbers and market talk, as Joe moves steadily forward, alone.
related_events: Radio broadcasts grain prices to Joe

name: Drum Majorettes Lead Parade Amid Ticker Tape Celebration
description: The drum majorettes marched at the front of the parade, moving down the city streets in precise formation. Above, people leaned out of skyscraper windows, tossing streams of ticker tape and confetti into the air. On the sidewalks, crowds joined in, throwing paper into the sky. The streets filled with swirling color and sound as the procession advanced through the city.
related_events: Drum majorettes lead parade through city streets
Crowd throws ticker tape and confetti during parade
related_occasions: Parade Celebration With Aerial Confetti Display

name: Charles Lindbergh Waves to the Crowd in Newsreel Clip
description: Amid a parade filled with drum majorettes, swirling ticker tape, and confetti falling from the sky, girls lean out of skyscraper windows, cheering. Intercut with the scene is a newsreel clip of Charles Lindbergh waving to the crowd, his hand rising and falling as he acknowledges the people gathered below.
related_events: Charles Lindbergh waves to crowd in newsreel clip
related_occasions: Parade Celebration With Aerial Confetti Display

name: Woodsy Admires New Hat and Carries Sally to Bed
description: Woodsy Niles stands at Sally Buck's dressing table, looking at himself in a new Stetson. He asks Sally if the hat fits. She smiles, and he lifts her off her feet, carrying her to the bed. They fall onto the covers together, laughing. Little Joe watches from nearby, his head buried in a beat-up cowboy hat.
related_events: Woodsy Niles admires himself in a new Stetson at Sally Buck's dressing table
Woodsy Niles lifts Sally Buck and carries her to the bed

name: Woodsy and Sally Fall on the Bed While Little Joe Laughs
description: Woodsy grabs Sally Buck, lifts her off her feet, and carries her to the bed. They fall across the covers together, laughing and struggling. Little Joe watches, his head buried in a beat-up cowboy hat, laughing with them. Sally protests, saying, "Woodsy Niles! The boy!" Woodsy replies, "He don't know what makes little apples by now, it's time he found out."
related_events: Little Joe laughs while Woodsy and Sally fall onto the bed
Sally Buck protests Woodsy Niles' actions due to Little Joe's presence
Woodsy Niles suggests Little Joe should learn about adult matters

name: Little Joe Gives Sally Buck a Neck Massage
description: In the middle of a busy day at the beauty parlor, Sally Buck sits with her eyes closed, resting wearily as little Joe massages her neck. She guides him with quiet instructions, asking him to press lower, then murmuring her approval as he adjusts. The hum of the parlor surrounds them—voices, tools, movement—while the two remain in their quiet moment, her song drifting softly over the noise: "...if that golden ring turns brass, Grammaw gonna buy you a looking glass..."
related_events: Little Joe massages Sally Buck's neck
Sally Buck directs little Joe to adjust neck massage

name: Sally Buck Sings a Lullaby in the Beauty Parlor
description: Sally Buck sits with her eyes closed, resting amid the bustle of the beauty parlor. Little Joe massages her neck, and she guides his hands, asking him to press a little lower. As the noise of the shop hums around them, she sings softly, her voice carrying a lullaby about a golden ring and a looking glass. The melody weaves through the air, blending with the sounds of the busy room.
related_events: Sally Buck sings a lullaby over beauty parlor noise

name: A Dishwasher, a Pinup Wall, and a Voice on the Loneliness of Women
description: A woman's voice speaks softly about a deep and growing problem shared by many women. The camera reveals a tabloid image of a naked woman captioned 'I BUY WHAT MY HUSBAND CAN'T GIVE,' pinned among other images of blonde women—rich, beautiful, or undressed—faded and damp above a dishwasher. Joe Buck scrapes food off plates, grinning at the wall. On a series of split screens, a lady commentator begins to speak about the shift in gender numbers since World War One, noting how women now outnumber men and control most of the nation's purchasing power. As she talks, lonely women slowly fill the surrounding screens. Joe reappears, stacking dishes, and chuckles, saying, 'Y'all, line up and take your turn.'
related_events: Sad woman's voice describes widespread personal problem
Camera reveals scandal sheet and pinup collection above dishwasher
Lady commentator becomes surrounded by lonely women in split screen

name: Joe Buck Cleans Dishes Amid Pinups and Women
description: Joe Buck scrapes food scraps from plates and stacks dishes near a dishwasher. On the wall above it, a collection of pinup images—women who are rich, beautiful, or naked, all blonde—hangs, their edges curled from steam. One image shows a naked woman beside her sleeping husband, with a caption reading I BUY WHAT MY HUSBAND CAN'T GIVE. Joe grins at the wall, then turns to the women around him, laughing gently as he tells them, 'Y'all, line up and take your turn.'
related_events: Joe Buck scrapes garbage while grinning at pinup pictures
Joe Buck stacks dishes while being surrounded by frustrated women
Joe Buck addresses frustrated women with tolerant laughter

name: Manager Points to Watch and Walks Away
description: The Manager points at his watch and tells Joe it's four to midnight. Joe tries to speak, saying he wants a word, but the Manager cuts him off, telling him later, maybe, and hurries away with a basket of dishes.
related_events: Manager points at watch and communicates deadline to Joe
Joe requests private conversation with Manager
Manager dismisses Joe and hurries away with dishes

name: Joe Says He's Leaving for the East
description: After the Manager hurries away with a basket of dishes, Joe tells Ralph he’s heading East. Ralph asks if he’s coming to work, and Joe says no, he’s just there for his day’s pay and to give notice. The Waitress appears at the door, calls out for cups, and leaves without seeing Joe. Ralph asks what Joe plans to do back East, and Joe says there are a lot of rich women there, though the men are mostly faggots, and that it must be a mess. Joe adds he sees no point in staying. When Ralph asks if he’ll collect his pay, Joe says he already has two hundred twenty-four dollars in cash and doesn’t need the Manager’s pay. He slaps his hip to show the money, then says the Manager can keep the pay or, if he isn’t man enough to take it himself, Joe would be happy to make him. Joe holds Ralph’s hand in a firm grip as they part.
related_events: Joe announces departure to the East and requests final pay
Ralph questions Joe about work attendance
Waitress calls for cups and exits without noticing Joe
Joe refuses final pay and expresses contempt toward Manager

name: Waitress Calls for Cups, Unaware of Joe
description: As Joe and Ralph talk, the Waitress steps into the doorway and calls out, 'Cups!' She turns and leaves without noticing Joe. The moment passes quickly, and the two men resume their conversation.
related_events: Waitress calls for cups and exits without noticing Joe

name: Joe Remembers the Beauty Parlor in Full Swing
description: Joe stands in front of the empty shop, his eyes catching the gilt-lettered sign glowing in the sunlight. For a moment, the silence breaks—not with present sound, but with echoes from the past. A girl’s laugh rings out, playful and close: 'Keep your meat hooks off my beauty operators, sugar.' The air fills with the clink of tools, the hum of driers, and Sally Buck’s voice singing, 'Hush, little baby, don't say a word, Grammaw gonna buy you a mockingbird...' The images form clearly—the crowded chairs, the chatter, the warmth of the place alive with motion and sound. Then the light shifts. The driers sit tarnished, the mirror is cracked, a FOR RENT sign taped in the glass. The sounds fade. Joe turns away, radio in hand, and walks toward the bus depot.
related_events: Joe recalls vivid memories of a bustling beauty parlor

name: Joe Leaves the Abandoned Beauty Parlor
description: The gilt-lettered sign in the window catches the sunlight, briefly masking the emptiness inside. Joe stands still, hearing echoes—a girl’s laugh, the phrase 'Keep your meat hooks off my beauty operators, sugar,' the chime of tools, Sally Buck’s voice singing 'Hush, little baby, don't say a word, Grammaw gonna buy you a mockingbird...' Then the light shifts. The tarnished driers, the cracked mirror, the FOR RENT sign become visible. Joe turns away, walks toward the bus depot, a radio pressed to his ear. The announcer says, 'Benson and Hedges One Hundreds makes special awards from time to time for anything that's longer than anything...' Joe mutters, 'Care to get out your yardstick, gentlemen?' A loud, familiar theme plays, blending with a flash of a Western film—Gary Cooper or John Wayne walking a dusty frontier street.
related_events: Joe turns away from the abandoned beauty parlor and heads toward the bus depot

name: Joe Listens to Radio and Mocks a Cigarette Ad
description: Joe walks down the street with a radio pressed to his ear. A voice announces that Benson and Hedges One Hundreds gives special awards for anything longer than anything else. Joe smirks and mutters, 'Care to get out your yardstick, gentlemen?' As he speaks, a bold orchestral theme blares from the radio, and a Western film plays nearby—its hero striding down a dusty frontier street.
related_events: Radio announcer promotes Benson and Hedges cigarette contest
Joe sarcastically responds to cigarette advertisement

name: Joe Hears Western Theme as Film Clip Plays
description: A loud, familiar variation of the 'Big Country' theme blares from the radio. On a nearby screen, a Western film clip shows a lone figure resembling Gary Cooper or John Wayne walking down a dusty frontier street. The music swells as the image flickers, casting a stark contrast to the quiet, empty street where Joe stands, radio in hand, before turning toward the bus depot.
related_events: Variant of 'Big Country' theme plays loudly and intercuts with Western film clip
Western film clip shows Gary Cooper or John Wayne walking a frontier street

name: Salesman Takes Seat and Shares His Sales Philosophy
description: A traveling salesman with badly-fitted dentures and a frayed collar sits beside Joe in the aisle seat. He begins talking about salesmanship, flipping through a worn leatherette notebook as his fingers twitch and his eyes dart nervously. He says it’s not the product, the price, or what you sell that matters—it’s personality. He boasts that he hasn’t shined his own shoes or shaved his own face in forty years, then leans in and tells Joe that the key is making people like you. If they do, he says, they’ll buy horsemeat believing it’s prime beef.
related_events: Traveling salesman takes aisle seat next to Joe and begins lecturing on salesmanship
Traveling salesman boasts about personal luxuries and lack of self-service
Traveling salesman proclaims golden rule of salesmanship to Joe

name: Salesman Calculates Expenses While Boasting About Success
description: The traveling salesman leans toward Joe in the aisle seat, his dentures clicking as he speaks with confidence about the secrets of selling. He boasts of never having shined his own shoes or shaved his own face in forty years, laughing as if to underline a life of luxury. At the same time, his fingers flip open a worn leatherette notebook, thumbing through columns of numbers. His eyes dart across the page, narrowing at each entry, while his other hand trembles slightly, pressing the edge of the notebook shut before opening it again. He continues talking, but his gaze keeps returning to the figures, tracing expenses with a twitching finger.
related_events: Traveling salesman calculates expenses in worn notebook

name: Joe gives a hesitant yes to the salesman
description: The traveling salesman leans toward Joe, his dentures slipping slightly as he talks about the power of personality in selling. He boasts about never having shined his own shoes or shaved his own face, pride in his voice. Joe looks at him, then nods faintly, muttering, 'Yeah, hell, yeah,' his voice flat, his eyes not quite meeting the man's.
related_events: Joe responds with hesitant agreement to salesman's claims

name: Singing and Stories on the Bus
description: Joe sits in the wide rear seat between two young Marines and a group of veterans wearing campaign caps and convention buttons. They pass a bottle and sing 'From the Balls of Montezuma to the Shores of Tripoli' in loud, uneven voices. Joe leans slightly forward, mirroring the posture of the men around him, his hands resting on his knees the way he once saw soldiers do. A veteran recalls being stationed at Kennedy and tells a story about a teenage girl in Pensacola, calling her 'jail bait -- but built?' and laughing as he describes a twenty-five dollar deal between three men. A marine responds with a crude joke about 'big peni-goddam-cillin bargain,' and the group erupts in laughter. Joe laughs too, hard and sudden, saying, 'Jesus goddam Christ, I ain't laughed so hard since I was out at Fort Benning, Georgia.' The marine turns to him and asks, 'Did you make the Viet?' Joe hesitates, then shakes his head. 'What? Oh, hell no. Motor pool mostly...'
related_events: Group passes bottle and sings military anthem during transit
Joe observes and silently adopts military demeanor during group interaction
Veteran shares risqué military anecdote during bus ride
Marine responds with crude wordplay to veteran's story

name: Sharing Stories on the Bus
description: A veteran on the bus recounts a risqué memory from his time stationed at Kennedy, describing a teenage girl in Pensacola he calls 'jail bait -- but built?' and mentions a twenty-five dollar deal between three men. A marine laughs and responds with a crude joke about 'big peni-goddam-cillin bargain,' and the group erupts in laughter. Joe leans into the moment, laughing along and saying, 'Jesus goddam Christ, I ain't laughed so hard since I was out at Fort Benning, Georgia.' The marine turns to him and asks, 'Did you make the Viet?' Joe hesitates, then shakes his head, saying, 'What? Oh, hell no. Motor pool mostly...'
related_events: Veteran shares risqué military anecdote during bus ride
Marine responds with crude wordplay to veteran's story
Joe recalls Fort Benning memory during group laughter

name: Joe's Vietnam Service Questioned by Marine
description: A Marine turns to Joe and asks, 'Did you make the Viet?' Joe hesitates, then shakes his head, saying, 'What? Oh, hell no. Motor pool mostly...' The laughter around him fades slightly as the men register his answer. The conversation moves on, but Joe sits quieter now, no longer joining in as the others resume their stories.
related_events: Marine questions Joe about Vietnam service
Joe denies combat experience and reveals motor pool role
Joe experiences emotional distancing after revealing non-combat role

name: Joe offers gum and makes a joke to a woman on the bus
description: Joe moves to the back of the bus and takes a seat in an empty double seat. He looks around at the other passengers—the old lady in front of him, the young sailor with acne behind, two teenage girls flirting with him, and a pale blonde woman across the aisle. She turns to him and asks for a stick of gum. Joe leans across the aisle, snaps his gum, and hands her one. She takes it gently, nibbling it between her front teeth. She thanks him and says she’s waiting for her Dramamine to kick in because she gets carsick. Joe says he only gets carsick on boats, then adds that it might be more about the fish smell than the motion. He notices her eyes are closed. He doesn’t say anything else.
related_events: Joe moves to his empty double seat at the back of the bus
Joe observes his fellow passengers' reactions to him
Joe offers gum to the pale blonde woman on the bus
Joe makes a joke about getting carsick on boats

name: Joe Lies Down and Withdraws into Himself
description: After the pale blonde closes her eyes, Joe stretches out across the empty double seat. He turns on the radio, but there is only static, and he snaps it off. He looks at his reflection in the bus window, squeezes a blackhead, and runs a comb through his hair. He picks a piece of tobacco from his tooth, lights a cigarette, and watches the flame die in the glass. The burnt match remains between his fingers as he stares out at a vast prairie, a solitary cowboy in the distance, a row of abandoned sharecropper shacks, and a barefoot little girl standing motionless by the road, watching the bus go by.
related_events: Joe stretches across both seats and turns on his radio
Joe examines his reflection and grooms himself
Joe lights a cigarette and stares at the passing landscape

name: Joe sits at the front and comments on the engine
description: Joe sits at the front of the bus, opposite the driver, and cracks his gum as he watches the billboards flash by. He listens to the hum of the tires and the roar of the engine, then says, "This is a powerful mothah, ain't it?" The driver does not respond. Joe gets up and walks to the back, leaving the front seat empty.
related_events: Joe comments on the bus's engine power

name: Joe Helps the Old Lady with Her Seat
description: Joe leans forward to help the old lady who is struggling with the release button on her seat. She scowls at him as he reaches over, then pulls her blanket tighter and turns away. Joe switches off her reading light. She tells him she wants it on. He turns it back on, offers a forced smile, and settles back into his seat.
related_events: Joe attempts to help the old lady with her seat release
Joe turns the old lady's reading light off and on

name: Joe Listens to Gospel Radio
description: Joe sits on a dark bus where most passengers are trying to sleep. A single reading light glows above the old lady in the seat ahead of him. He fiddles restlessly, turning on a radio that plays a revivalist gospel broadcast. A preacher's voice fills his ears, speaking about investing in Jesus and how money answers all things. The voice promises a free leatherette hymn book to anyone who sends a dollar to the Evangelical Congregation of the Air. Joe remembers his grandmother Sally Buck telling him to say his prayers. He leans forward to help the old lady with her seat release when she struggles, but she scowls at him, pulls her blanket tight, and turns away. Joe switches off her light, then switches it back on when she demands it. He settles back, the radio still playing, and notices an old cowhand sitting across the aisle, watching him with quiet curiosity.
related_events: Joe listens to a revivalist gospel group on the radio

name: Joe Offers a Light to the Old Cowhand
description: Joe notices the Old Cowhand looking at his clothes with a curious gaze. The man quickly looks away when their eyes meet. After a pause, Joe strikes a match on his thumb and holds it across the aisle to light the Old Cowhand's cigarette. The man coughs as he inhales, then wipes his eyes with a faded bandana.
related_events: Old cowhand observes Joe's clothing with curiosity
Joe offers a light to the old cowhand

name: Joe Jokes and Asks About Woodsy Niles
description: The Old Cowhand coughs harshly after lighting the cigarette Joe offered a match for, then wipes his watery eyes with a faded bandana. Joe chuckles and says, 'You throw in Sister Rosella and you got a deal, right, old timer?' The Old Cowhand gives a faint, humorless smile. Joe leans back and asks if he’s ever come across a cowman named Woodsy Niles, saying he’s a friend of his grammaw, Sally Buck. The Old Cowhand thinks for a moment, then shakes his head. Joe leans back, laughing quietly to himself.
related_events: Old Cowhand coughs while inhaling smoke from a cigarette
Old Cowhand wipes his eyes with a faded bandana
Joe jokes about Sister Rosella with the Old Cowhand
Joe asks the Old Cowhand about Woodsy Niles

name: Joe Asks About Woodsy Niles and Laughs Off the Silence
description: Joe asks the Old Cowhand if he’s ever come across a cowman named Woodsy Niles, a friend of his grammaw Sally Buck. The Old Cowhand considers the question, then shakes his head. Joe leans back in his seat, laughing quietly to himself.
related_events: Old Cowhand shakes his head in response to Joe's question
Joe laughs to himself after the conversation
